definition: Love — deep affection, covenant loyalty, divine and human love
etymology: From root א-ה-ב (ʔ-h-b). Proto-Semitic *ʔhb 'to love, desire'. Cognate with Akkadian râmu, Ugaritic ʔhb. In the MT used for both divine love (Deut 7:8) and human love (Gen 29:20).
textual_variants: DSS 1QIsaᵃ: identical root form
LXX consistently renders as ἀγάπη

definition: Faithfulness, firmness, steadfastness — trustworthiness and reliability
etymology: From root א-מ-ן (ʔ-m-n) 'to be firm, confirmed'. Proto-Semitic *ʔmn 'to be true'. Source of 'Amen'. Cognate with Arabic ʔamīn, Akkadian umānu.
textual_variants: Habakkuk 2:4 — DSS reads אמונתו (his faithfulness); MT identical

definition: Hope, expectation — literally 'a cord', hence something stretched toward the future
etymology: From root ק-ו-ה (q-w-h) 'to wait, look for'. Related to cord/line (Josh 2:18). Proto-Semitic *qwh 'to gather, wait'.
textual_variants: Jer 29:11 — consistent across MSS

definition: Grace, favour, elegance — gracious disposition, unmerited kindness
etymology: From root ח-נ-ן (ḥ-n-n) 'to be gracious'. Proto-Semitic *ḥnn 'to show favour'. Cognate with Arabic ḥanān 'compassion', Akkadian enēnu.
textual_variants: Gen 6:8 — uniform across witnesses

definition: Light — both physical light and metaphorical divine illumination
etymology: From root א-ו-ר (ʔ-w-r) 'to be luminous'. Proto-Semitic *ʔwr 'light, fire'. Cognate with Akkadian urru 'daylight', Ugaritic ʔr.

definition: Life, lives — life in its fullness, both physical and spiritual
etymology: From root ח-י-ה (ḥ-y-h) 'to live'. Proto-Semitic *ḥyw 'to live'. Cognate with Arabic ḥayāt, Akkadian balāṭu. Always plural in Hebrew (lives).
textual_variants: Gen 2:7 — 'breath of life' consistent

definition: Truth, faithfulness, reliability — what is firm, certain, dependable
etymology: From root א-מ-ן (ʔ-m-n) 'to be firm'. Proto-Semitic *ʔmn. Related to emunah and amen. Connotes stability and trustworthiness rather than abstract truth.
textual_variants: Ps 119:160 — consistent across witnesses

definition: Way, road, path, journey — manner of life, moral course
etymology: From root ד-ר-ך (d-r-k) 'to tread, march'. Proto-Semitic *drk 'to tread'. Cognate with Akkadian darāku, Arabic daraka.
textual_variants: Ps 1:6 — 'way of the righteous' consistent

definition: Peace, completeness, soundness, welfare — wholeness in every dimension
etymology: From root ש-ל-ם (š-l-m) 'to be complete, whole'. Proto-Semitic *šlm. Cognate with Arabic salām, Akkadian šalāmu. Encompasses physical, relational, and spiritual well-being.
textual_variants: Isa 9:6 — 'Prince of Peace' consistent across MSS

definition: Spirit, wind, breath — the animating force; Spirit of God; human spirit
etymology: From root ר-ו-ח (r-w-ḥ) 'to breathe'. Proto-Semitic *rwḥ 'wind, spirit'. Cognate with Arabic rūḥ, Akkadian šāru. 378 occurrences in OT.

definition: Soul, self, life, person, desire — the whole living being
etymology: From root נ-פ-שׁ (n-p-š) 'to breathe'. Proto-Semitic *npš 'throat, breath, life'. Cognate with Akkadian napištu 'life, throat', Ugaritic npš.
textual_variants: Gen 2:7 — 'living soul' consistent; LXX renders as ψυχή

definition: Flesh, body, meat — human/animal flesh; mankind; kinship
etymology: From root ב-שׂ-ר (b-ś-r). Proto-Semitic *bśr 'flesh, skin'. Cognate with Arabic bašar 'skin, mankind', Akkadian bašāru.
textual_variants: Gen 2:23 — 'flesh of my flesh' uniform across witnesses

definition: God, mighty one — the supreme deity; generic term for divine being
etymology: Proto-Semitic *ʔil 'god, deity'. One of the oldest Semitic words. Cognate with Akkadian ilu, Ugaritic ʔl, Arabic ʔilāh (→ Allāh). Head of the Canaanite pantheon.
textual_variants: El Shaddai, El Elyon — compound forms across MSS

definition: Lord, master, sovereign — title of authority, applied to God and humans
etymology: Proto-Semitic *ʔdn 'lord'. Cognate with Ugaritic ʔadn, Phoenician ʔdn (→ Greek Adonis). Adonai is the plural of majesty form.
textual_variants: Ps 110:1 — both YHWH and Adonai used; MSS consistent

definition: Son, child, descendant — offspring; member of a group ('sons of Israel')
etymology: From root ב-נ-ה (b-n-h) 'to build'. Proto-Semitic *bn 'son'. Cognate with Arabic ibn, Akkadian māru, Aramaic bar.
textual_variants: Ps 2:7 — 'You are my Son' consistent across witnesses

definition: Father, ancestor, originator — patriarch, God as Father
etymology: Proto-Semitic *ʔab 'father'. One of the most universal Semitic terms. Cognate with Arabic ʔab, Akkadian abu, Ethiopic ʔab.
textual_variants: Mal 2:10 — 'one Father' consistent

definition: King, ruler, sovereign — royal authority, kingship
etymology: From root מ-ל-ך (m-l-k) 'to reign'. Proto-Semitic *mlk 'king, to rule'. Cognate with Akkadian malku, Ugaritic mlk, Arabic malik.

definition: Law, instruction, teaching — divine direction; the Pentateuch
etymology: From root י-ר-ה (y-r-h) 'to throw, shoot, direct'. Proto-Semitic *wrh 'to show, direct'. Originally 'instruction/guidance' rather than rigid law.

definition: Water, waters — both literal and symbolic (chaos, purification, life)

textual_variants: Gen 1:2 — 'upon the face of the waters' uniform

definition: Earth, land, ground, country — the physical world; the promised land
etymology: Proto-Semitic *ʔarṣ́ 'earth'. Cognate with Akkadian erṣetu, Ugaritic ʔarṣ, Arabic ʔarḍ. 2,504 occurrences — one of the most frequent nouns in OT.
textual_variants: Consistent across all witnesses

definition: Heaven, heavens, sky — the visible heavens; the abode of God
etymology: Proto-Semitic *šamāʔ 'sky, heaven'. Cognate with Akkadian šamû, Ugaritic šmm, Arabic samāʔ. Always dual/plural in Hebrew.
textual_variants: Gen 1:1 — consistent across all witnesses

definition: Death — physical death; the realm of the dead (Sheol)
etymology: From root מ-ו-ת (m-w-t) 'to die'. Proto-Semitic *mwt 'death'. Cognate with Ugaritic Mot (god of death), Akkadian mūtu, Arabic mawt.
textual_variants: Hos 13:14 — 'O death, where are your plagues' consistent

definition: Sin, sin offering — missing the mark; both the act and the remedy
etymology: From root ח-ט-א (ḥ-ṭ-ʔ) 'to miss, go wrong'. Proto-Semitic *ḫṭʔ. Cognate with Arabic ḫaṭiʔa 'to err'. Literally 'missing the target' (cf. Judg 20:16).
textual_variants: Gen 4:7 — 'sin crouches at the door' consistent

definition: To redeem, buy back, act as kinsman-redeemer
etymology: Proto-Semitic *gʔl 'to redeem'. Key concept: the goel (kinsman-redeemer) has legal obligation to buy back family property and avenge blood.

definition: Salvation, deliverance — rescue from danger; divine saving act
etymology: From root י-שׁ-ע (y-š-ʕ) 'to save, deliver'. Proto-Semitic *wṯʕ. Source of name Yeshua/Jesus. Cognate with Arabic wasaʕa 'to be wide/spacious' — salvation as spaciousness.
textual_variants: Ex 14:13 — 'salvation of the LORD' uniform

definition: Lovingkindness, mercy, covenant loyalty — steadfast love that endures

definition: Word, thing, matter — spoken utterance; divine decree; event/affair

textual_variants: Consistent across all witnesses

definition: Priest — one who officiates at worship; mediator between God and people
etymology: From root כ-ה-ן (k-h-n). Proto-Semitic *khn 'to be a priest'. Cognate with Arabic kāhin 'soothsayer', Akkadian kumru.
textual_variants: Consistent across witnesses

definition: Covenant, alliance, pledge — solemn agreement between God and people
etymology: Possibly from root ב-ר-ה (b-r-h) 'to eat' (covenant meals) or Akkadian birītu 'fetter, bond'. Proto-Semitic debated. The central organizing concept of the Hebrew Bible.

definition: Holy, sacred, set apart — separated for divine purpose
etymology: From root ק-ד-שׁ (q-d-š) 'to be set apart'. Proto-Semitic *qdš. Cognate with Akkadian qadištu, Ugaritic qdš. Primary meaning: separation from the profane.
textual_variants: Isa 6:3 — 'Holy, holy, holy' (trisagion) consistent across MSS

definition: Prophet — one called to speak for God; foreteller and forth-teller

definition: Justice, judgment, ordinance — legal decision; right order; custom
etymology: From root שׁ-פ-ט (š-p-ṭ) 'to judge'. Proto-Semitic *ṯpṭ 'to judge'. Cognate with Akkadian šapāṭu, Ugaritic ṯpṭ.

definition: Mercy, compassion — deep tender feelings; womb-love (from rechem, womb)

definition: Grace, favour, kindness — unmerited divine influence on the heart; gratitude

definition: Soul, life, self — the seat of feelings and emotions; the inner person

definition: Water — both literal and symbolic (baptism, living water, purification)

definition: Earth, land, soil, ground — the physical world; a country or territory

etymology: PIE *ph₂tḗr 'father'. One of the most stable PIE words. Cognate with Greek πατήρ, Sanskrit pitṛ, English 'father', German Vater.
textual_variants: 'Pater noster qui es in caelis' — consistent

definition: King — 'Rex Iudaeorum' (King of the Jews); 'Rex Regum' (King of Kings)
etymology: PIE *h₃reǵ- 'to straighten, direct, rule'. Cognate with Sanskrit rājā, Irish rí, English 'right', 'regal'.
textual_variants: 'Rex Iudaeorum' — consistent across all witnesses

definition: Law — legal statute; the Mosaic Law (Lex Mosaica)
etymology: PIE *leǵ- 'to gather, collect' (law as collected rules). Source of English 'legal', 'legislature'.
textual_variants: Consistent rendering of νόμος

definition: Water — baptismal water; 'living water' (aqua viva)
etymology: PIE *h₂ekʷeh₂ 'water'. Cognate with Gothic aƕa 'water'. Source of English 'aqua', 'aquatic'.
textual_variants: 'spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas' — consistent

definition: Earth, land, ground — the physical world; territory
etymology: PIE *ters- 'dry' (earth as dry land vs sea). Source of English 'terrain', 'territory'.
textual_variants: 'in principio creavit Deus caelum et terram' — consistent

definition: Heaven, sky — 'regnum caelorum' (Kingdom of Heaven)
etymology: PIE *keh₂id- 'bright' or from caedō 'to cut' (sky as vault). Source of English 'celestial'.
textual_variants: caelum vs coelum — orthographic variant; both attested

definition: Death — physical death; spiritual death; personified Death
etymology: PIE *mr̥tis, from *mer- 'to die'. Cognate with Sanskrit mṛtyu, English 'murder', 'mortal'.
textual_variants: 'ubi est mors victoria tua' (1 Cor 15:55) — consistent

definition: Resurrection — rising from the dead; a Christian Latin coinage
etymology: From re- 'again' + surgere 'to rise'. PIE *h₃reǵ- 'to straighten'. Not used in classical Latin — Christian coinage.
textual_variants: Consistent Christian Latin coinage across all Vulgate MSS

definition: Gospel, good news — the Christian message of salvation
etymology: Borrowed directly from Greek εὐαγγέλιον (euangelion). Not native Latin. Source of English 'evangelical'.
textual_variants: Consistent across all Vulgate witnesses

definition: Sacrament, sacred mystery, oath — military oath; Christian mystery/rite
etymology: From sacer 'sacred' + -mentum. Originally a military oath or deposit. Tertullian first used it for Christian rites. Jerome uses it for Greek μυστήριον (mystērion).
textual_variants: Eph 5:32 — 'sacramentum hoc magnum est' for Greek μυστήριον

definition: Glory, fame, renown — divine splendour; 'Gloria in excelsis Deo'
etymology: PIE *gneh₃- 'to know' (glory as being known). Cognate with Greek κλέος 'fame'. Jerome renders δόξα (doxa) as gloria.
textual_variants: 'Gloria in excelsis Deo' (Lk 2:14) — consistent

definition: Justice, righteousness — moral rightness; divine vindication
etymology: From iūstus 'just, righteous'. PIE *h₂yew- 'law, oath'. Jerome renders δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosyne) as iustitia.
textual_variants: Gen 15:6 — 'reputavit ei ad iustitiam' consistent

definition: Mercy, compassion, pity — tender-heartedness; having a heart (cor) for the wretched (miser)
etymology: From miser 'wretched' + cor/cordis 'heart'. Literally 'having a heart for the wretched'. A beautiful Latin compound. Jerome renders ἔλεος (eleos) as misericordia.
textual_variants: Consistent across all Vulgate witnesses

definition: Sin, offense, fault — moral transgression; a stumbling
etymology: From peccare 'to stumble, sin'. PIE *ped- 'foot' (sin as tripping). Cognate connection debated. Jerome renders ἁμαρτία (hamartia) as peccatum.
textual_variants: Consistent rendering of ἁμαρτία

definition: Redemption, ransom — buying back; liberation through payment
etymology: From redimere 'to buy back' (re- + emere 'to buy'). PIE *h₁em- 'to take'. Jerome renders ἀπολύτρωσις (apolytrōsis) as redemptio.
textual_variants: Rom 3:24 — 'per redemptionem quae est in Christo' consistent

definition: Salvation, health, safety — rescue; well-being; greeting (salve!)
etymology: PIE *solh₂- 'whole, well-kept'. Cognate with salvus 'safe', English 'safe', 'salvation'. Jerome renders σωτηρία (sōtēria) as salus.
textual_variants: Consistent rendering of σωτηρία

definition: Charity, love, dearness — divine love; the highest virtue (1 Cor 13)
etymology: From cārus 'dear, beloved'. PIE *keh₂- 'to desire'. Jerome's preferred translation of ἀγάπη in 1 Cor 13 and epistles. Source of English 'charity'.
textual_variants: 1 Cor 13:13 — 'nunc autem manet fides spes caritas' consistent

definition: Word — the divine Word (Verbum); 'In principio erat Verbum' (John 1:1)
etymology: PIE *werdʰo- 'word'. Cognate with English 'word', German Wort, Gothic waurd. Jerome renders λόγος (logos) as verbum in John's prologue.
textual_variants: 'In principio erat Verbum' — consistent across all Vulgate witnesses

definition: Church, assembly, congregation — borrowed from Greek ἐκκλησία
etymology: Borrowed directly from Greek ἐκκλησία (ekklēsia) 'assembly'. Not native Latin. Source of English 'ecclesiastical'. Jerome renders ἐκκλησία as ecclesia.
textual_variants: Consistent across all Vulgate witnesses

definition: Prophet — one who speaks for God; borrowed from Greek
etymology: Borrowed from Greek προφήτης (prophētēs). Source of English 'prophet'. Jerome renders προφήτης as propheta.
textual_variants: Consistent across all witnesses

definition: Priest — one who performs sacred rites; 'sacerdos in aeternum' (priest forever)
etymology: From sacer 'sacred' + dare 'to give' (one who gives/performs sacred things). PIE *seh₂k- (sacred) + *deh₃- (give).
textual_variants: Ps 110:4 — 'tu es sacerdos in aeternum' consistent

definition: Testament, covenant, will — binding agreement; 'Novum Testamentum' (New Testament)
etymology: From testārī 'to witness'. PIE *tris-to- 'third party, witness'. The Latin term emphasizing the legal/testamentary aspect. Jerome renders διαθήκη (diathēkē) as testamentum.
textual_variants: Consistent across Vulgate witnesses

definition: Holy, sacred, saint — consecrated, set apart; 'Spiritus Sanctus' (Holy Spirit)
etymology: From sancīre 'to make sacred'. PIE *seh₂k- 'to sanctify'. Cognate with sacer 'sacred'. Jerome renders ἅγιος (hagios) as sanctus.
textual_variants: 'Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus' (Isa 6:3) — consistent

definition: Kingdom, reign — 'Regnum Dei' (Kingdom of God); royal power
etymology: From rex 'king'. PIE *h₃reǵ- 'to rule'. Source of English 'reign'. Jerome renders βασιλεία (basileia) as regnum.
textual_variants: 'Regnum Dei' / 'Regnum caelorum' — consistent

definition: Cross — instrument of execution; 'crux Christi' (Cross of Christ)
etymology: PIE *krewk- 'cross, pole'. Possibly cognate with Old Norse hrúga 'heap'. Originally a torture instrument; transformed into central Christian symbol.
textual_variants: 'tollat crucem suam' — consistent
